title: Two-path recovery: scheduled pg_dump artefact PLUS vendor point-in-time recovery, both elicited, both required
description: The recovery model is two-path and both paths are required at v1.0.0: (a) a scheduled export runner drives pg_dump via child_process.execFile against the elicited connection URL, writes the artefact to the elicited destination (a filesystem path, an S3 URL, an operator-owned path), and emits a backupExported lifecycle event carrying the artefact path and a completion timestamp; (b) the deploy target's own point-in-time recovery is enabled and its cadence and retention window are elicited (a managed Postgres cluster's PITR window, a self-managed cluster's WAL-archive posture). Neither path is optional. A fresh Postgres primed from a pg_dump artefact reads the rows committed at or before the artefact's completion timestamp; a fresh Postgres restored to a PITR point reads the rows committed at or before that point. The recovery-destination is elicited at apply time (a filesystem path, an S3 URL, or an operator-owned path). The recovery-cadence is elicited (daily is the shipped default; hourly is the higher-frequency alternative; weekly is the lower-frequency alternative, per ADR-2804). The pitr-provider path is elicited (hosted vendor PITR, or self-managed WAL archiving); both paths are required together at v1.0.0.
rationale: pg_dump gives a portable artefact the operator can move off the deploy target; PITR gives the fine-grained restore point pg_dump cannot. Neither alone covers the two failure classes a shipped Postgres project has to survive: a corrupted managed cluster (PITR helps only if the corruption pre-dates the retention floor; a pg_dump artefact off-cluster survives cluster loss) and a data-integrity incident an operator wants to unwind by minutes (PITR restore point; a nightly pg_dump loses too much). Two paths, both required, is the general-enterprise-practice shape.
